title: mcp-server cannot reach db-api: all BigQuery-backed MCP tools fail
description:
The standalone mcp-server (/mcp path, used by external MCP clients) has NEVER been able to reach db-api, so every BigQuery-backed tool returns 'BigQuery API URL not configured'.

Confirmed failing live on daly (2026-07-21): query_bigquery, get_bigquery_schema, get_asm_qtl_by_gene, get_open_chromatin_by_gene, get_variant_effect_by_gene.

Two independent causes, BOTH must be fixed:
1. BIGQUERY_API_URL is set in k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml but has never existed in k8s/deployments/mcp-server.yaml (git log -S confirms no commit ever added it).
2. NetworkPolicy allow-ingress-db-api (k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml:137-151) admits only app=chat-backend; monitor-policy.yaml adds monitor. mcp-server is not permitted, so even with the env var set the call would be blocked.

Manifests are profile-independent => affects finngen AND daly equally.

chat-backend is unaffected (has the env var and is allowed by policy), so the web UI agent's BQ tools work; only the standalone MCP server is impacted.

Note these tools are BigQuery-by-design: results-api has no by-gene open_chromatin endpoint, so executor.py:824 resolves gene->coords via gene_annotations_v.

Decision needed: opening db-api to mcp-server is a network-isolation change, not just a config fix.

title: Phase 0: decide ChromBPNet row-scale thresholding policy
description: Count ChromBPNet variant-score rows (132 contexts x variants, potentially billions). Decide thresholding (significant/non-zero only, or top-N per context) before sizing tabix/BQ. Biggest scale risk. Gates the Marderstein munge task.
design:
RECOMMENDED DEFAULT thresholding policy (empirical cutoff + row counts to be CONFIRMED once data is downloaded — blocked on .1). Keep this task OPEN.
Problem: ChromBPNet = 132 contexts x all variants (~3 billion predictions in the paper). Do NOT store the full cross-product.
Default:
- ChromBPNet -> variant_effect (model=chrombpnet), LONG. Emit a row only for (variant, context) pairs that pass a significance/effect threshold, NOT all 132 contexts per variant. Prefer the per-context significance calls provided by the Synapse release if present; else keep per-context empirical mlog10p >= 3 (p <= 1e-3) OR abs(chrombpnet_logfc) in the top 1 percent per context. Always set is_significant and mlog10p so the cutoff is transparent and re-filterable.
- Retain a variant if significant in ANY context (so by_variant lookups return it); emit its passing contexts, plus optionally its single top context.
- FLARE -> variant_effect (model=flare): keep the FULL released FLARE prioritized-variant set (already curated and far smaller); pan-context rows with cell_type/tissue NULL.
Rationale: bounds storage to variants with a real predicted effect somewhere (millions, not billions) — exactly what the query needs. Empirical step (after .1): count rows at this cutoff, confirm the significance fields the release actually provides, adjust cutoff to a sane table size.
close_reason: Decision made: default thresholding policy adopted (recorded in --design). Empirical row-count confirmation happens inside the Marderstein munge task (.13), which applies and tunes the default; no separate gate needed.

title: [mcp-server] Serve MCP OAuth discovery (.well-known/oauth-protected-resource + WWW-Authenticate)
description:
Repo: ../genetics-mcp-server. File: src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py, in the ASGI auth_middleware (same place /healthz is special-cased).

Implement RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata so MCP clients (Claude connectors, ChatGPT, brainzzz) auto-discover the authorization server:
- Serve GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (and the path-suffixed /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp) returning JSON: { resource: OAUTH_RESOURCE_URL, authorization_servers: [OAUTH_ISSUER], scopes_supported: [...], bearer_methods_supported: ["header"] }. Serve it WITHOUT requiring a bearer token.
- On a 401 from the bearer middleware, add header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<resource>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" so clients know where to look.
Only enable these when OAUTH_ISSUER is configured. The authorization-server metadata itself (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) is served by Keycloak, not here.

Depends on the settings subtask.

title: Feature: Direct OAuth (Keycloak) auth for MCP server — GeneGenie / brainzzz
description:
Let external web applications (first: brainzzz) connect to the GeneGenie MCP server via a standard OAuth 2.1 flow, instead of a shared api-token. Add this as a FOURTH bearer-validation path alongside the existing three (MCP_API_KEY shared secret, Google Identity Token JWT, per-user API token) — nothing existing is removed.

WHY: IAP/Google ID-Tokens don't fit a third-party app acting on behalf of its own users (audience-bound, no consent/refresh, users not on our email allow-list). MCP's HTTP transport defines an OAuth 2.1 profile where the MCP server is an OAuth *resource server* and clients auto-discover the *authorization server*. The daly/GeneGenie deployment already runs Keycloak as a full OIDC AS (https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics, ENABLE_KEYCLOAK on for daly), so Keycloak is the authorization server and a 'web application type' OAuth client registered there is exactly what's needed.

SCOPE: GeneGenie (daly profile) only for now. finngen/FinnGenie has Keycloak OFF (Google-direct) and is out of scope.

DESIGN CONTRACT (shared across subtasks):
- Authorization server = Keycloak realm 'genetics'; issuer https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics.
- MCP resource canonical URL (RFC 8707 resource indicator / RFC 9728 resource identifier) = https://genegenie.broadinstitute.org/mcp.
- Keycloak issues access tokens (JWT) with aud including that resource URL (via an audience mapper / dedicated client scope on the brainzzz client).
- MCP server validates: signature via Keycloak JWKS, iss match, aud includes resource URL, exp; THEN the existing email/domain allow-list (settings.allowed_emails / allowed_email_domains, already fed by the bearer-auth-allowed ConfigMap).
- Discovery: MCP server serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728) pointing at the Keycloak issuer, and returns WWW-Authenticate: Bearer with resource_metadata=... on 401. The authorization-server metadata itself is served by Keycloak (already on auth.<domain>).

Code work is split between the sibling repo ../genetics-mcp-server (validation + discovery + settings) and this repo genetics-results-suite (deployment env + auth-gateway routing + docs). Plus Keycloak client config (ops).

title: Phase 0: finalize EpiMap 18-state storage + open/active state set
description: Decide how the ChromHMM 18-state label is stored (score_type=chromhmm_18state + state token placement) and which states count as open/active (TSS/enhancer/transcribed). Gates the EpiMap munge task.
design:
EpiMap ChromHMM 18-state modeling for the open_chromatin product.
Model = Roadmap/EpiMap 18-state (observed_aux_18), 833 biosamples, hg38 CALLS.
INCLUDE (accessible/active regulatory subset) as open_chromatin rows:
  active promoter: TssA, TssFlnk, TssFlnkU, TssFlnkD
  active enhancer: EnhA1, EnhA2, EnhG1, EnhG2, EnhWk
  poised/bivalent (accessible, tagged): TssBiv, EnhBiv
EXCLUDE (not open peaks): Tx, TxWk, ZNF_Rpts, Het, ReprPC, ReprPCWk, Quies.
State storage (NO schema change): encode the exact state in score_type as chromhmm:<State> (e.g. score_type=chromhmm:EnhA1); assay=chromHMM; score=NULL (presence-based — ChromHMM is a categorical segmentation, so row existence = state called in that biosample).
Agent-facing regulatory_class grouping (map in the MCP tool description, NOT stored): Tss* -> promoter, Enh* -> enhancer, *Biv -> bivalent.
Labels: cell_type = verbatim EpiMap biosample name; tissue from EpiMap sample metadata (GROUP/Anatomy column); life_stage=adult unless the biosample metadata marks it fetal/embryonic; condition=unknown.
Do NOT import EpiMap DNase layer (that is the Meuleman DHS index, which was dropped).
close_reason: Resolved: EpiMap active/accessible state subset + state-in-score_type encoding decided. Decision recorded in --design.

title: Phase 0: confirm genome builds & liftOver needs
description: Confirm all sources vs hg38: Marderstein/Li/Catlas/ROSMAP snATAC and EpiMap ChromHMM CALLS are hg38; Calderon is hg19 (needs liftOver). Verify EpiMap hg38 CALLS are used, not hg19. Gates all munge tasks.
design:
Genome-build decision — platform standard = GRCh38/hg38 (GENCODE).
- marderstein (scATAC peaks + ChromBPNet + FLARE): hg38, native, no liftOver.
- li_brain_atac (Li 2023 Science): hg38, native.
- catlas (Zhang 2021 Cell): hg38, native (verify cCRE BED header at download).
- epimap (Boix 2021): USE the hg38 CALLS directory (ChromHMM observed_aux_18_hg38), NOT hg19.
- calderon_immune (Calderon 2019): hg19 -> liftOver to hg38 (UCSC hg19ToHg38.over.chain); drop unmapped and split/multi-mapping intervals, then re-sort.
- rosmap_brain (Xiong 2023): hg38, native.
RULE for every munge task: verify the source file build at download; if hg19, liftOver to hg38 and drop unmapped/multimapped before bgzip+tabix. Only Calderon is known-hg19 today.
close_reason: Resolved: builds determined (all hg38 except Calderon hg19->liftOver; EpiMap use hg38 CALLS). Per-file verification folded into each munge task. Decision recorded in --design.

title: Optional: full ChromBPNet variant_effect run (common/rare/ldsc classes)
description: MAY NOT BE NEEDED. Currently marderstein_chrombpnet is loaded from only the small asd wide matrix (~160MB, validates the streaming reshape end-to-end). The full ChromBPNet release (Synapse syn64713923) also has common (12GB), rare (16.6GB), ldsc (19GB) wide per-variant matrices — ~48GB download total, each >100GB uncompressed. This is a DATA-COMPLETENESS step only, not a code/feature gap: the --product chrombpnet path already streams+reshapes wide->long in bounded batches. FLARE (pan-context prioritized score, quantile_rank) is already fully loaded and answers the 'is this variant predicted to disrupt accessibility / how strongly' question, so full ChromBPNet is likely unnecessary; it only adds finer per-cell-type abs_logfc coverage for common/rare/ldsc variants.
design: Run (from genetics-results-munge, needs Synapse creds + ~48GB download + disk): python3 scripts/munge_marderstein.py --product chrombpnet --download --cbp-name-filter 'common|rare|ldsc' --output <DATA_DIR>/marderstein_chrombpnet.tsv.gz --cbp-batch-rows 100000  (or point --chrombpnet at pre-downloaded wide files). Thresholding defaults: --mlog10p-thresh 3.0, --top-quantile 0.01. Then gsutil cp the .tsv.gz + .tbi to gs://finngen-commons/results_api_data/variant_effect/marderstein/ (and the daly bucket), and reload variant_effect in BigQuery. Gate: only do this if per-cell-type ChromBPNet breadth beyond asd + FLARE is actually requested.
